items.title: The Constitution of India, 1950: Preamble, Fundamental Rights and Duties, Directive Principles, federal structure with three legislative lists.
Parliament is the Lok Sabha (543 elected seats) and the Rajya Sabha (245, representing the states and union territories).
The Finance Commission is appointed every five years under Article 280 to divide taxes between the Union and the states.
The Goods and Services Tax from 1 July 2017 replaced a maze of central and state indirect taxes; the GST Council decides rates by weighted vote.
United Nations founded 1945: General Assembly, Security Council with five permanent members and ten elected, ICJ at The Hague.
G20 is nineteen countries plus the European Union and the African Union, which joined in 2023; India hosted the 2023 summit in New Delhi.
India is a dialogue partner of ASEAN and a member of the East Asia Summit, ASEM and the Indian Ocean Rim Association.
The Non-Aligned Movement began at Bandung in 1955 and was formalised at Belgrade in 1961; India was a founding voice.
India has 28 states and 8 union territories; states were reorganised on linguistic lines by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
Panchayati Raj under the 73rd Amendment gives three tiers of rural local self-government with reservations for SC, ST and women.
The Inter-State Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, settles disputes and coordinates policy between the Union and the states.
Article 355 requires the Union to protect every state against external aggression and internal disturbance.
The three services are the Indian Army, Indian Navy and Indian Air Force, with the Indian Coast Guard under the Ministry of Defence.
The Chief of Defence Staff, created in 2019, integrates the three services; the Department of Military Affairs was formed alongside.
Agnipath recruits soldiers for four years with a Seva Nidhi package and a reserved quota in central armed police forces.
India's nuclear doctrine: no first use, credible minimum deterrence and civilian control of the strategic forces.
The Election Commission of India was established on 25 January 1950, the day the Constitution came into force.
The Tenth Schedule is the anti-defection law: a member who defies a party whip on a confidence or money vote can lose the seat.
The President is elected by an electoral college of elected MPs and elected MLAs by proportional representation with a single transferable vote.
The Governor is appointed by the President for a five-year term and holds reserve, assent and report powers under Articles 155-162.
The Reserve Bank of India, founded 1935, is the central bank: it issues currency, manages reserves and supervises banks.
Monetary policy is set by the Monetary Policy Committee, six members, with an inflation target of 4% within a band of plus or minus 2%.
The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 requires the Union and the states to publish fiscal policy statements.
Securities and Exchange Board of India, given statutory powers in 1992, regulates the capital market.
Five-year plans ran from 1951 to 2017; the NITI Aayog, formed in 2015, now sets the medium-term strategy.
1991 liberalisation: the rupee moved to a market-determined rate, tariffs fell, foreign investment was opened and industrial licensing was scrapped.
The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 guarantees 100 days of wage employment a year to rural households.
Direct Benefit Transfer sends subsidies to bank accounts linked to Aadhaar, cutting leakage.
India has seven land neighbours: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Afghanistan.
The Line of Control separates India and Pakistan in Jammu and Kashmir; the Line of Actual Control separates India and China.
SAARC has eight members; BIMSTEC links Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
The Indus Waters Treaty, 1960 divides the Indus system rivers, with the World Bank as intermediary.
ISRO was founded on 15 August 1969; its launch vehicles are the PSLV, GSLV Mk II and the heavy-lift LVM3.
Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south polar region on 23 August 2023, and Aditya-L1 studies the Sun from the first Lagrange point.
The Department of Atomic Energy runs the nuclear power programme, from the first reactor at Trombay to the Kudankulam units.
The Digital Public Infrastructure stack — Aadhaar, UPI and DigiLocker — is now cited internationally as a model.
The Quad brings India, the United States, Japan and Australia together on maritime security and vaccines in the Indo-Pacific.
BRICS was founded in 2006 and expanded in 2024; it is a forum for cooperation among major emerging economies.
India borders the Indian Ocean on three sides; the Andaman and Nicobar Command is its only tri-service theatre command.
The Malabar exercise began as a bilateral India-US drill in 1992 and is now a four-nation annual exercise.
The Padma awards — Vibhushan, Bhushan and Shri — are announced on 26 January each year by the President.
The National Cadet Corps was raised in 1948 under the NCC Act and has Army, Navy and Air wings.
The National Service Scheme runs the motto 'Not Me But You' and is the country's largest student volunteer programme.
The Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award; the Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award.
1947-48, 1965 and 1971: the three Indo-Pak wars; the 1971 war ended with the creation of Bangladesh.
The 1962 war with China was followed by the Himalayan climbing season of 1965 and the Siachen deployment of 1984.
Operation Cactus, 1988 restored the government of the Maldives; Indian forces have served in UN missions since 1950.
Kargil in 1999 was fought along the Line of Control at altitude; the Vijay Diwas observance marks its end on 26 July.
